holidays.name: International Panic Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace your inner alarmist. Flail your arms, run in small circles, and shout about nothing in particular. It's a tongue-in-cheek reminder that some days are just made for freaking out.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance with unclear origins, and it's usually traced to internet and humor culture. It has been listed on June 18 for years.
holidays.funFact: The word 'panic' comes from the Greek god Pan. Ancient Greeks believed his sudden shouts from the wilderness could send whole armies running in terror.

holidays.name: International Sushi Day
holidays.description: A day for rolling, dipping, and chopstick-wielding. Sushi fans around the world celebrate with nigiri, maki, sashimi, and whatever creative rolls their local restaurant has dreamed up.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food holiday that appeared in the 2000s and has spread through social media. It celebrates sushi's journey from a Japanese fermented-fish preservation method to a global favorite.
holidays.funFact: The earliest form of sushi was fish packed in fermented rice to preserve it. The rice was thrown away and only the fish was eaten.

holidays.name: International Picnic Day
holidays.description: Grab a blanket, a basket, and some snacks, and eat outside. The day invites you to take your lunch to a park, a beach, or even your backyard.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's often linked to a famous 1989 picnic on the Hungarian-Austrian border, but that event was on August 19.
holidays.funFact: The word 'picnic' may come from the 17th-century French 'pique-nique'. Early picnics were potluck-style gatherings where each guest brought something to share.
